channel.title: Build With the Memory
channel.description: A working developer's devlog on building with AI coding agents: committed markdown memory networks and a self-improving loop.

item.title: I said state machine and lost people
item.description: Four lines added to Pillar 14, because I had been describing the simplest file in the method with the most technical phrase I own.

item.title: A gate below an exit is a comment
item.description: The check standing between my private network and a public picture of it had never run. Not once. It was written correctly and placed four lines too low.

item.title: One word different
item.description: The project got a new name, one word different. Renaming is mostly not the name. It is every place the old one is written down.

item.title: A picture with none of the words
item.description: I wanted to show the shape of my memory network without showing what is in it. Then I found the gate that was supposed to stop leaks had been passing everything for weeks.

item.title: The network knew why, but not what
item.description: Pillar 14. A memory network records decisions well and current state badly, and the gap is where agents guess.

item.title: A thirteenth pillar
item.description: Borrowed memory. Reading what other teams wrote down, without letting it start giving your agent orders.

item.title: The repo is public
item.description: The repo was private while I wrote it. As of this week it isn't.

item.title: Why this repo exists
item.description: Every AI session starts from nothing. This is the way of working that stopped me from losing the same context over and over.
